title: Nouns 4: Making Plurals with -а and -я
description: Two groups of Russian nouns form their plurals with -а or -я instead of -ы / -и. Neuters are regular: -о → -а, -е → -я (окно → окна, море → моря). A small set of masculines is irregular and high-frequency: дом → дома, город → города, профессор → профессора, учитель → учителя.
descriptionRussian: Две группы русских существительных образуют множественное число не на -ы / -и, а на -а или -я. Среднее правило простое: -о → -а, -е → -я (окно → окна, море → моря). Небольшая группа мужских — исключения, но очень частотные: дом → дома, город → города, профессор → профессора, учитель → учителя.
intro: Not every plural takes -ы or -и. One group of nouns reaches for -а or -я instead, and it splits neatly in two: a set that behaves exactly as you would predict from lesson 1, and a set you simply have to know. The second group is short and stubborn, full of words like дом and город that you will say every day. It also carries a stress shift, and with these words the stress is not decoration. It is part of the form.
rules: Neuter plurals are regular: -о becomes -а, -е becomes -я. Examples: окно → окна, письмо → письма, слово → слова, море → моря, поле → поля.

A small but high-frequency set of masculine nouns takes stressed -а (or -я) in the plural instead of the expected -ы. Core A1 list: дом → дома, город → города, доктор → доктора, профессор → профессора, лес → леса, поезд → поезда, голос → голоса, глаз → глаза, адрес → адреса, паспорт → паспорта, цвет → цвета, учитель → учителя.
The irregular masculine -а / -я plurals are end-stressed: дома́, города́, доктора́, учителя́. The stress shifts from the singular stem to the plural ending.
Watch the дома trap: дома́ (end-stressed) is the plural 'houses', but до́ма (stem-stressed) is the everyday adverb 'at home'. Same letters, different stress, different meaning.
There is no general rule for which masculine nouns belong to this irregular set. Learn each member together with its plural form when you meet it.
examples: окно → окна. (Neuter -о regularly becomes -а in the plural.)
море → моря. (Neuter -е regularly becomes -я in the plural.)
письмо → письма. (Neuter -о → -а; the plural is stressed differently from the singular, as often happens with neuters.)
дом → дома́. (Irregular masculine; end-stressed plural. Not the expected домы, which does not exist.)
учитель → учителя́. (Irregular masculine, end-stressed. The -я ending replaces -а because Russian spelling never writes -а directly after soft -ь. The form учители is archaic.)
город → города́. (Same irregular set as дом; end-stressed. Городы does not exist in modern Russian.)

tables.title: Irregular masculine plurals (the A1 set to memorise)

items.hint: Neuter -о becomes what in the plural?
items.explanation: Neuter -о regularly becomes -а in the plural: окно → окна. Neuter nouns never take -ы or -и; they have their own swap.

items.hint: Neuter -е becomes what in the plural?
items.explanation: Neuter -е regularly becomes -я in the plural: море → моря.

items.hint: Same rule as окно. Neuter -о goes to what?
items.explanation: Neuter -о becomes -а in the plural: слово → слова. (As often with neuters, the stress shifts in the plural, but the spelling rule is simple.)

items.promptEnglish: Tall houses are standing on the street.
items.hint: Дом is one of the irregular masculines. What ending does it take?
items.explanation: Дом is in the irregular masculine set that takes stressed -а in the plural: дома́.

items.hint: Same irregular set as дом. What plural does город take?
items.explanation: Город belongs to the same irregular set as дом, лес, профессор: stressed -а in the plural (города́).

items.hint: Учитель is in the irregular set, but with -я (because of the soft sign). Pick the end-stressed form.
items.explanation: Учитель takes the irregular -я plural: учителя́ (end-stressed). It takes -я rather than -а because Russian spelling never writes -а directly after soft -ь.

blanks: На улице стоят высокие _____. (Tall houses are standing on the street.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Дом belongs to the small irregular set of masculines that take stressed -а in the plural: дома́. Other members of the set include город (города), доктор (доктора), профессор (профессора), лес (леса), учитель (учителя, with -я).

errorCorrection.sentence: В театре хорошие место рядом со сценой.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The theatre has good seats near the stage.
errorCorrection.explanation: Место is neuter (-о ending); the plural takes -а: места. The adjective 'хорошие' is already plural, signalling that the noun must also be plural. The neuter -о → -а pattern is the standard plural for -о nouns.

errorCorrection.sentence: Старые поезды стоят в этом музее.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Old trains stand in this museum.
errorCorrection.explanation: Поезд is masculine consonant, but it belongs to the small set that takes the STRESSED -а́ plural (not the expected -ы): поезд → поезда́. Other members: дом → дома́, город → города́, лес → леса́. Поезды does not exist.

errorCorrection.sentence: Новые доктор пришли в нашу больницу на этой неделе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: New doctors have arrived at our hospital this week.
errorCorrection.explanation: Доктор is masculine, and it belongs to the irregular -а́ plural set: доктор → доктора́. The plural adjective 'новые' signals that the noun must be plural too.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Old houses are on the street.
minimalPairs.explanation: Дом is in the irregular set that takes stressed -а in the plural (дома́). The expected -ы form (домы) is not a real Russian word. The rule for this small group simply has to be memorised.
Город belongs to the same irregular set as дом: plural города́ (end-stressed). Городы does not exist in modern Russian.
Учитель takes the irregular -я plural учителя́ (end-stressed). Учители is archaic and is not used in everyday modern Russian, even though it would be the 'regular' soft-sign form.
Окно is neuter, and neuter -о regularly becomes -а in the plural: окна. Neuter nouns never take -ы; that ending is reserved for hard masculines and feminine -а stems. Окны is not a Russian word.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each noun by which plural pattern it follows: regular neuter (-а / -я), irregular masculine (-а / -я), or regular masculine (-ы).

reviewVocab.definition: the regular pattern for neuter nouns: -о → -а, -е → -я.
reviewVocab.example: Окно → окна. Море → моря. Письмо → письма.

reviewVocab.definition: a closed set of common masculines that take stressed -а instead of -ы (учитель takes -я because -а cannot follow soft -ь). A1 core: дом, город, доктор, профессор, лес, поезд, голос, глаз, адрес, паспорт, цвет, учитель.
reviewVocab.example: Дом → дома́. Город → города́. Учитель → учителя́.

reviewVocab.definition: дома́ (end-stressed) is the plural 'houses'. До́ма (stem-stressed) is the adverb 'at home'. Same letters, different stress, different meaning.
reviewVocab.example: Я до́ма. В городе красивые дома́.
